name: Kyanite
physical: Traditionally associated with relaxation of tension
Said to bring a balanced, aligned feeling
Crystal healers link it with ease in the throat and neck
summary: Kyanite forms blue blades with two hardnesses, a self-clearing stone in crystal lore for alignment, honest communication and quick calm in meditation.
intro: Kyanite grows as long, bladed crystals that look like shards of blue sky, usually in shades from pale ice to deep sapphire, with a pearly sheen along the flat faces. Its most remarkable feature is anisotropy: it has a hardness of about 4 along the length of a blade and about 7 across it, so a knife can scratch one direction but not the other. Crystals frequently show uneven colour banding, with deep blue cores and white edges. It often appears in schist alongside garnet and staurolite. In crystal circles the blades are loved as wands and fans, and the stone is often described as one of the most reliable meditation aids.
history: The name kyanite comes from the Greek kyanos, meaning deep blue, and was applied in 1789 by the German geologist Abraham Werner. It is also called disthene, from the Greek for two strengths, a reference to its directional hardness. Industrial kyanite has long been used to make heat-resistant ceramics and spark plugs, because it converts to mullite at high temperatures. In gem jewelry it appears as cabochons and faceted stones from Nepal, Brazil and Tanzania, although perfect cleavage makes it tricky for cutters. Deep sapphire-blue crystals from Nepal are admired by collectors and often sold as Himalayan kyanite.
meaning: In the crystal tradition kyanite is a stone of alignment and clear communication. Practitioners link it with the throat and third eye chakras and say it brings all the energy centres into harmony quickly and gently. It is one of the few stones commonly said never to hold negativity and never to need cleansing, though many people still tidy their collections. It is used for speaking truth calmly, easing arguments and finding calm in the middle of busy days. Meditators like blue kyanite blades for their ability to quiet the mind swiftly. Physically it is traditionally associated with relaxation and balance, and with ease in the throat and neck, as a comfort stone only.
howToUse: Hold a kyanite blade in each hand in meditation and breathe slowly, imagining a blue line of light running through your spine. Place a blade on the throat chakra before a presentation or a difficult chat. Use kyanite wands to sweep gently around the body in energy-clearing exercises. Place one on a nightstand to wind down, or keep a piece near a work computer to promote clear thinking. In grids, arrange blades like rays around a clear quartz point to extend its energy outward.
care: Kyanite is brittle and easily scratched along its length, so handle blades gently. Avoid soaking, as some specimens include minerals that may degrade, and skip ultrasonic cleaners. Wipe with a soft dry or barely damp cloth. Many practitioners say kyanite needs no cleansing, but smoke, sound or moonlight are gentle options. Sunlight is fine for charging. Store blades in padded containers, apart from harder stones like quartz that can scratch the surface.
identify: Kyanite forms flat, bladed crystals with perfect cleavage and its signature unequal hardness. Colours range from pale blue to deep cobalt, often with white streaks. Look-alikes include sapphire, tanzanite, iolite, dyed quartz and glass. Dye or blue coating is sometimes used on poor-quality material, giving an unnaturally even or fluorescent colour. Real kyanite shows pearly lustre and has a distinctive mixed hardness. Gem-quality stones may show a chatoyant effect. Buy from reliable dealers who describe origin and treatments.

faq.a: Tradition holds that kyanite does not hold on to negative energy and needs little or no cleansing. Many people still give it a gentle smoke or moonlight clear for peace of mind.

faq.q: Why does kyanite have two hardnesses?
faq.a: Its atoms are arranged unevenly, so the crystal is softer along its length than across its width. That is why a knife can scratch a blade lengthwise but not across it.
In crystal tradition kyanite supports clear communication, calm and chakra alignment. It is a popular meditation companion and is linked with the throat and third eye.
